title: Unit fractions: equal pieces of a whole
subtitle: Divide a whole into equal parts and describe the size of one part.
challenge: A ribbon of length 1 meter is cut into 5 identical pieces. What fraction of the ribbon is each piece?
predictionPrompt: If the ribbon was cut into 10 pieces instead of 5, would each piece be larger or smaller?
formalDefinition: A unit fraction 1/n is one part when the whole is split into n equal parts; n must be a positive whole number. More equal parts of the same whole means smaller individual parts.

steps: Partition the unit interval [0, 1] into 5 equal sub-intervals.
Summing all 5 parts restores the whole: 1/5 + 1/5 + 1/5 + 1/5 + 1/5 = 5/5 = 1.
workedExample.result: Every proper fraction m/n is simply m copies of the unit fraction 1/n.

misconception.mistake: 1/8 is larger than 1/4 because 8 is larger than 4.
misconception.correction: The denominator indicates division: cutting a pie into 8 slices yields smaller slices than cutting into 4.

reflection: Unit fractions are the elemental basis of all rational numbers. Understanding 1/n grounds all fraction arithmetic.
prerequisiteCheck: A whole must be identified and the parts must be equal. Can four unequal ribbon pieces each be called one fourth?
representation: Mark 0 and 1 on a strip. Put equally spaced marks at 1/5, 2/5, 3/5, and 4/5. One step has length 1/5; the endpoint is 5/5 = 1.

faded.prompt: A metre is divided into 6 equal pieces. One piece is __ of a metre. Four pieces are __ of a metre.
faded.solution: One piece is 1/6 metre; four pieces are 4/6 = 2/3 metre.

independent.prompt: Which is larger: 1/7 or 1/4, using the same whole?
independent.solution: 1/4 is larger because the whole is divided into fewer equal pieces.

independent.prompt: How many copies of 1/8 make one whole?

explanation: Explain why denominators must be positive here, why 1/0 is undefined, and why equal-sized parts matter. You do not need a calculus argument about limits.

transfer.prompt: A 2-metre ribbon is divided into 8 equal pieces. What fraction of the ribbon is one piece, and what length is it?
transfer.solution: One piece is 1/8 of the ribbon but 2/8 = 1/4 metre long. Fraction of the whole and measured length are different quantities.

retrieval: Tomorrow sketch a number line and locate 1/3. After a week, explain why 1/9 < 1/6 without a calculator.
